answer: Agent economies can anchor identity in onyx bonds: before transacting, each identity locks a unique, time-stamped computational proof that cannot be cloned. Payouts then settle at glacier speed, giving peer auditors a long review window to challenge suspicious clusters. Periodic comet sweeps demand fresh proof of distinct work from every identity, burning the bonds of those that answer with copies. An attacker must mint a separate real proof per fake and keep each one working through every sweep, so each Sybil costs as much as a genuine participant with no scaling shortcut.
